As the new school year begins, more Americans are expressing support for banning students from using phones during the entire school day.

As the new school year begins, the voices supporting a phone ban in schools continue to grow

That's right, it's only July now, but for some reason, summer has already ended. My kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow — this is the second year in a row that school has started before August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion: eligible students and educators who purchase select Mac and iPad models before August 27 can receive a gift card of up to $150. Consumers in several US states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

Although back-to-school discounts are extremely popular, the use of smartphones in the classroom is increasingly being met with intolerance.

The most-liked comment was posted by user bibliophilecode

As a high school student, when my school implemented a phone ban last year, I had only one thought — the ban needed to be tightened further. Our current classroom-time ban (which does not include lunch and study periods) is sometimes not enforced by teachers or students, but when the ban is strictly enforced, the results are very significant. I can't count how many people's grades have slipped because they were distracted by playing games during class.

A new survey from the Pew Research Center found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during school hours. This figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Currently, only 18% of people oppose the classroom ban.

Support for a stricter all-day ban — prohibiting phone use from first period to last period — has risen even faster. For the first time, more Americans support than oppose banning phone use for the entire school day.

The survey also noted that although support has risen across all age groups since 2024, younger adults remain less enthusiastic about both classroom and all-day bans. Click here to read the full report.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use only during class time, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
